en: Feeling shame or guilt.

ashamed.ety: From Middle English ashamed, aschamed, from Old English āsċamod, past participle of Old English āsċamian (“to be ashamed”), equivalent to a- + shame + -ed.

ex.en: The man was ashamed of being born poor.
ex.ja: その男は貧しく生まれたことを恥ずかしく思っていた。

ex.en: I'm ashamed to go out dressed like this.
ex.ja: こんな身なりで外出するのは気が引ける。

ex.en: I'm not ashamed of my father being poor.
ex.ja: 私は父が貧しいことを恥ずかしいとは思わない。

note.ja: a（強意）+ shamed（恥じた）。古英語 āscamian。「恥じている」。shame と同じ。

en: A small ball placed in a container to cast a vote; now, by extension, a piece of paper or card used for this purpose, or some other means…
The process of voting, especially in secret; a round of voting.
To vote or decide by ballot.
To draw lots.

ballot.ety: Borrowed from Italian balota (obsolete), ballotta (“small ball, especially one used to register a vote”), from balla (“bale, bundle”) + -otta (suffix forming diminutive nouns); or from Middle French balote (obsolete), ballotte (“small ball used to register a vote”) (also compare Middle French balotiage, French ballottage (“second ballot, runoff”)); both ultimately from Proto-West Germanic *ballu (“ball”), from Proto-Germanic *balluz (“ball”).

ex.en: Voters cast their ballots for mayor every four years.
ex.ja: 市長選は４年ごとに行われる。

ex.en: International observers counted up the ballot.
ex.ja: 国際監視団は投票の集計をしました。

note.ja: イタリア語 ballotta（小さな玉）から。玉を投じて投票した →「投票（用紙）」。

en: A place where the dead are buried; a graveyard or memorial park.

cemetery.ety: From Middle English cimiterie, from Old French cimitiere, from Medieval Latin cimitērium, from Late Latin coemētērium, from Ancient Greek κοιμητήριον (koimētḗrion), from κοιμάω (koimáō, “I put to sleep”); compare cœmeterium. Displaced Middle English charnel (“mass grave, cemetery”) and Old English līctūn (“cemetery”).

ex.en: Let's go through the cemetery. It's closer that way.
ex.ja: 墓地を抜けよう。その方が近いよ。

ex.en: I used to walk in the cemetery in my youth.
ex.ja: 若い頃墓地をよく歩いたものだ。

ex.en: Let's go through the cemetery. It's shorter that way.
ex.ja: 墓地を抜けよう。その方が近いよ。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 koimētērion（眠る場所）から。koiman（寝かせる）。「死者が眠る場所」→「墓地」。

en: To violate rules in order to gain, or attempt to gain, advantage from a situation.
To be unfaithful to one's spouse or partner; to commit adultery, or to engage in sexual or romantic conduct with a person other than one'…
An act of deception or fraud; that which is the means of fraud or deception.
Someone who cheats.

ex.en: I'd been cheated out of my life savings!
ex.ja: 一生かかって蓄えた貯金をだまし取られてしまったのだった。

ex.en: The man cheated her out of her money.
ex.ja: 男は彼女をだましてその金を取り上げた。

ex.en: A moral person doesn't lie, cheat, or steal.
ex.ja: 道徳的な人はうそをついたりだましたり盗んだりしない。

note.ja: escheat（土地の没収）の短縮。役人が不正に財産を没収したことから →「だます・不正をする」。

en: A cheerful attitude; happiness; a good, happy, or positive mood.
That which promotes good spirits or cheerfulness, especially food and entertainment prepared for a festive occasion.
To gladden; to make cheerful; often with up.
To infuse life, courage, animation, or hope, into; to inspirit; to solace or comfort.

cheer.ety: From Middle English chere, from Anglo-Norman chere, from Old French chiere (“head, face; appearance; reception, hospitality; meal, dinner, food”) (Modern French chère), from Late Latin cara (“head”).

ex.en: I cheered myself up by listening to music.
ex.ja: 音楽を聞いて気を晴らした。

ex.en: Cheer up! Everything will soon be all right.
ex.ja: 元気を出せ。そのうちすべてうまくいくだろう。

ex.en: The last three blocks! Come on! Cheer up!
ex.ja: 残り３ブロックだ、がんばれ！

note.ja: 古フランス語 chiere（顔）から。「顔つき」→「上機嫌」→「声援」。

en: An agreement or contract.
To form an agreement or contract.
Closely packed or densely constituted; having much material in a small volume.
Having all necessary features fitting neatly into a small space.

ex.en: I'd like to rent a compact car.
ex.ja: 小型車を借りたいのですが。

ex.en: The compact edition is a lower price.
ex.ja: 縮刷版は安価だ。

ex.en: The compact edition doesn't cost as much.
ex.ja: 縮刷版は安価だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 compactus（固められた）から。com + pangere（固定する）。「ぎっしり詰まった・小型の」。「協定」も同じ語。

en: A visit to consult somebody, such as a doctor; a consultation.
To seek the opinion or advice of another; to take counsel; to deliberate together; to confer; to advise.
To advise or offer expertise.

consult.ety: From Middle French consulter, from Latin cōnsultum, from cōnsultus, from cōnsulō.

ex.en: I consulted with my father about the plan.
ex.ja: その計画について父に相談した。

ex.en: You should consult a doctor at once, George.
ex.ja: ジョージ、きみはすぐに医者に見てもらうべきだよ。

ex.en: I consulted with my sister about my marriage.
ex.ja: 私は結婚のことで姉に相談した。

note.ja: ラテン語 consulere（相談する）から。→「相談する・（辞書などを）調べる・診察を受ける」。

en: Deficiency in amount or quality; a falling short; lack.
A situation wherein, or amount whereby, spending exceeds (e.g. government) revenue.

deficit.ety: From French déficit, from Latin dēficit. Related to defect.

ex.en: How huge a deficit can the nation stand?
ex.ja: どのくらい莫大な赤字に国家は耐えられるのだろうか。

ex.en: The government is running its largest deficit ever.
ex.ja: 政府は史上最大の赤字をかかえています。

ex.en: He made up the deficit with a loan.
ex.ja: 不足を借金で補充した。

note.ja: ラテン語「不足している」（deficere ＝ de（離れて）+ facere（する））から。→「赤字・不足」。

en: A demonstration or visual explanation.
A recording of a song meant to demonstrate its overall sound for the purpose of getting it published or recorded more fully.
designed to test consumers' interest in a retail item prior to purchasing.
To record a demo version of (a song).
To demonstrate.

demo.ety: Clipping of demonstration and various other words beginning with "demo-".

ex.en: The salesperson gave us a demo of the new phone.
ex.ja: 販売員は新しい携帯電話の実演をしてくれた。

note.ja: demonstration の短縮。ラテン語 demonstrare（はっきり示す）。monster と同じ語根。

en: An evil being resident in or working for Hell; a devil.
A false god or idol; a Satanic divinity.

demon.ety: From Middle English demon, a borrowing from Medieval Latin dēmōn, daemōn (“lar, familiar spirit, guardian spirit”), from Ancient Greek δαίμων (daímōn, “dispenser, god, protective spirit”). Displaced native Old English sċucca (“evil spirit”) and Old English þyrs (“ogre or monster”). Doublet of daimon; also more distantly a doublet or piecewise doublet of time.

ex.en: There are no demons in this world.
ex.ja: この世に鬼はいない。

ex.en: I want to be the demon next!
ex.ja: 次は僕が鬼になりたい！

ex.en: I want to become a demon next!
ex.ja: 次は僕が鬼になりたい！

note.ja: ギリシャ語 daimōn（神霊）から。→「悪魔・鬼」。

en: The act of demonstrating; showing or explaining something.
An event at which something will be demonstrated.

demonstration.ety:
From Middle English demonstracioun, from Old French demonstration, from Latin dēmōnstrātiōnem, from dēmōnstrāre (“show or explain”), from dē- (“of or concerning”) + mōnstrāre (“show”).
Morphologically demonstrate + -ion.

ex.en: The police tried to stop the street demonstration.
ex.ja: 警察は街頭デモを阻止しようとした。

ex.en: He took part in the anti-war demonstration.
ex.ja: 彼はその反戦デモに参加した。

ex.en: Secret police moved among the crowd during the demonstration.
ex.ja: デモの最中秘密警察が人込みの中を動きまわった。

note.ja: de（完全に）+ monstr（示す）+ ation。はっきり示すこと →「実演・証明・デモ」。

en: To discover or notice, especially by careful search, examination, or probing.
To work or solve cases as a detective.

detect.ety:
From Latin detectus, perfect passive participle of detegere (“to uncover or disclose”), from de- + tegere (“to cover”); see tegument, tile, thatch.
Sense "to work or solve cases as a detective" a back-formation from detective.

ex.en: We detected a great fault in the system.
ex.ja: その組織の大欠陥を見つけた。

ex.en: The computer can detect 200 types of error.
ex.ja: そのコンピューターは２００種類の間違いを探せる。

ex.en: I've detected a big mistake.
ex.ja: 私は大きな誤りを見つけた。

note.ja: de（取り去る）+ tect（覆う）。覆いを取る →「見つける・検出する」。protect（前を覆う→守る）と対。

en: The act or process of detecting, uncovering, or finding out, the discovery of something new, hidden, or disguised.
The act or process of finding or detecting an electrical signal in a carrier wave.

detection.ety: Learned borrowing from Latin dētēctiō. By surface analysis, detect + -ion.

ex.en: She had escaped detection somehow.
ex.ja: 彼女はどうにか見つけ出されずにすんだ。

note.ja: de + tect + ion。覆いを取ること →「発見・検出」。detective（探偵）。

en: A small figure resembling a human being that is used as a toy.
A good-natured, cooperative or helpful person.
Synonym of doll up.

doll.ety:
From Doll, pet form of the given name Dorothy.
Etymology 1, noun sense 7 was coined and popularized by American writer Jacqueline Susann in 1966 through her book Valley of the Dolls (1966) and the film adaptation Valley of the Dolls (1967).

ex.en: Show me the doll that you bought yesterday.
ex.ja: 君が昨日買った人形を見せてください。

ex.en: The old man gave her a small doll.
ex.ja: その老人は彼女に小さい人形をあげました。

ex.en: This is a doll which she made herself.
ex.ja: これは彼女が自分で作った人形だ。

note.ja: 女性の名 Dorothy の愛称 Doll から。「人形」。

en: Having been given freely rather than purchased.

ex.en: The amount donated still falls short of the goal.
ex.ja: 募金はまだ目標額に達しない。

ex.en: He donated a lot of money.
ex.ja: 彼は大金を寄付した。

ex.en: Have you ever donated blood?
ex.ja: 献血をしたことがありますか。

note.ja: donate（寄付する）+ -ed。ラテン語 donare（与える）。

en: Complex, detailed, or sophisticated.
Intricate, fancy, flashy, or showy.
Тo develop in detail or complexity.
To expand/enlarge in detail.

elaborate.ety: 1575, from Late Latin ēlabōrātus (“worked out”), past participle of ēlabōrō (“to work out”), from ē- (“out, forth, fully”) + labor (“work, toil, exertion”). More at e-, labour.

ex.en: Let's take time out to elaborate a strategy.
ex.ja: タイムをとって作戦を練ろう。

ex.en: His theory is based on elaborate investigation.
ex.ja: 彼の理論は入念な調査に基づいている。

ex.en: Could you elaborate on your new theory?
ex.ja: あなたの新しい理論について詳しく話していただけますか。

note.ja: e（外へ）+ labor（働く）+ ate。働いて作り出した →「手の込んだ・詳しく述べる」。

en: Great skill or knowledge in a particular field or hobby.
Advice, or opinion, of an expert.

expertise.ety:

ex.en: This is outside my area of expertise.
ex.ja: これは、私の専門外だ。

ex.en: It's outside my expertise.
ex.ja: 自分の領域外にある。

note.ja: ex（完全に）+ pert（試す）+ ise。試し尽くして得たもの →「専門知識・専門技術」。expert（専門家）。

en: A single elongated piece of a given material, roughly round in cross-section, often twisted with other fibers to form thread.
A material in the form of fibers.

fiber.ety: From French fibre, from Old French fibre, from Latin fibra.

ex.en: You need to eat more fiber.
ex.ja: もっと繊維質を取りなさい。

ex.en: He was lacking in moral fiber.
ex.ja: 彼は道徳力に欠けていた。

ex.en: Please cut perpendicular to the fibers.
ex.ja: 繊維に対して直角に切ってください。

note.ja: ラテン語 fibra（繊維）から。→「繊維・食物繊維・ファイバー」。

en: Cooked by frying.
Fried with the yolk unbroken.

ex.en: Fried food usually doesn't agree with me.
ex.ja: 揚げ物は私の体質に普通合わないんだ。

ex.en: I don't often eat deep-fried food.
ex.ja: 揚げ物はめったに食べません。

ex.en: Today, I had fried rice for lunch.
ex.ja: 今日の昼はチャーハンを食べた。

note.ja: fry（揚げる・炒める）の過去分詞。ラテン語 frigere（焼く）。

en: Retail foodstuffs and other household supplies.
A shop or store that sells groceries; a grocery store.
To go grocery shopping.
To furnish with groceries.

grocery.ety: From Middle English grocerye, equivalent to grocer + -y. Compare gross. Doublet of groceria.

ex.en: They sell many types of food and grocery products.
ex.ja: あそこでは多くのタイプの食品や雑貨を売っている。

ex.en: I am in the grocery line.
ex.ja: 食料品商をやっている。

ex.en: There used to be a grocery store around the corner.
ex.ja: 昔はかどに食料品店があったものだ。

note.ja: grocer（食料雑貨商）+ -y。grocer はもと「大口（gross）で売る商人」。gross と同じ語源。

en: Half of the way between two points.
Moderately; somewhat.
Middle; midway; being in the middle of the way or distance.

halfway.ety:
From Middle English halfwey, from Old English healfweġ (“half-way”), equivalent to half- + way. Compare partway.
Cognate with Saterland Frisian hoolfwais (“halfway”), Dutch halfweg (“halfway”), German halbwegs (“halfway”), Danish halvvejs (“halfway”), Swedish halvvägs (“halfway”).

ex.en: Let's meet halfway between your house and mine.
ex.ja: 君の家と私の家の中間で落ち合うことにしよう。

ex.en: My car broke down halfway to your house.
ex.ja: 君んちに行く途中で、車が故障しちゃった。

ex.en: I don't want you to do things halfway.
ex.ja: 中途半端なことはしないで欲しい。

note.ja: half（半分）+ way（道）。「道の途中で」。

en: The outer covering of a fruit or seed.
Any covering.
To remove the outer covering of a fruit or seed.

hull.ety:
From Middle English hul, hulle, holle (“seed covering, hull of a ship”), from Old English hulu (“seed covering”), from Proto-Germanic *hul-, perhaps from Proto-Indo-European *ḱel- (“to cover, hide”); or possibly from Proto-Indo-European *kal- (“hard”).
Compare Dutch hul (“hood”), German Hülle (“cover, wrap”), Hülse (“hull”); also Old Irish calad, calath (“hard”), Latin callus, callum (“rough skin”), Old Church Slavonic калити (kaliti, “to cool, harden”). For the sense development, compare French coque (“nutshell; ship's hull”), Ancient Greek φάσηλος (phásēlos, “bean pod; yacht”).

ex.en: The ship's hull was badly damaged in the storm.
ex.ja: その船の船体は嵐でひどく傷ついた。

note.ja: 古英語 hulu（さや）から。「さや・殻」→「船体」。

en: In an independent manner.

independently.ety:
Etymology tree
English independent
Middle English -ly
English -ly
English independently
From independent + -ly.

ex.en: Tom and Bill arrived at the conclusion independently of each other.
ex.ja: トムとビルは別々に考えて同じ結論に達した。

ex.en: After the bushfires, we have independently decided to call off this year's fireworks display.
ex.ja: 山火事の後なので今年の花火大会は自主的に中止を決定しました。

note.ja: independent（独立した）+ -ly。in（否定）+ dependent（依存した）、de + pendere（ぶら下がる）。「独立して」。

en: An act of pointing out or indicating.
A fact that shows that something exists or may happen.

indication.ety: From Old French indication, from Latin indicātiō (“a showing, indicating the value of something; valuation”), from indicō (“point out, indicate, show; value”); see indicate; compare French indication, Spanish indicación, Italian indicazione. By surface analysis, indicate + -ion.

ex.en: There is no indication that it will rain today.
ex.ja: 今日は雨が降りそうな気配はない。

note.ja: in（〜へ）+ dic（示す）+ ation。指し示すこと →「兆候・指示・表示」。

en: To hold up a claim emphatically.
To demand continually that something happen or be done; to reiterate a demand despite requests to abandon it.

insist.ety:
Partly from Middle French insister, from Latin īnsistere; and partly from a back-formation from insistence.
Compare typologically from the same PIE root Bulgarian настоявам (nastojavam), Russian наста́ивать (nastáivatʹ).

ex.en: The doctor insisted that he stay in bed.
ex.ja: 医者は、彼が寝ているようにと強く言った。

ex.en: I insisted that we change our original plan.
ex.ja: 私は、我々の原案を変更すべきことを主張した。

ex.en: They will insist on her staying there longer.
ex.ja: 彼らは、彼女がもっと長くそこに滞在するようにと主張するだろう。

note.ja: in（上に）+ sist（立つ）。（自分の考えの）上に立ち続ける →「主張する・言い張る」。

en: Done with intensity or to a great degree; thorough.
Being made more intense.
A thing which makes something more intense; specifically (linguistics), a form of a word with a more forceful or stronger sense than the …
A course taught intensively, involving much activity in a short period of time.

intensive.ety: The adjective is derived from Late Middle English intensive (“fervent, great, intense”), borrowed from Old French intensif, intensive (modern French intensif) + Middle English -ive (suffix meaning ‘of the nature of, relating to’ forming adjectives), equivalent to intense + -ive. Intensif is from Medieval Latin intēnsīvus, from Latin intēnsus (“attentive; eager, intent; intensive”) + -īvus (suffix forming adjectives with the sense ‘doing; related to doing’); and intēnsus is the perfect passive participle of intendō (“to stretch out, strain”), from in- (prefix meaning ‘to, towards’) + tendō (“to

ex.en: Extensive reading is as important as intensive reading.
ex.ja: 多読は精読と同様重要である。

ex.en: The intensive course did wonders for my French.
ex.ja: 集中講習で私のフランス語は驚くほど上達した。

ex.en: Capital-intensive industries are not necessarily knowledge-intensive industries.
ex.ja: 資本集約産業は必ずしも知識集約産業ではない。

note.ja: intense（強烈な）+ -ive。「集中的な」→ intensive care（集中治療）。

Offering or involving interaction with the user.
A feature (as in a museum) that can be interacted with.

ex.ja: その科学館には体験型の展示がたくさんある。

en: Closely acquainted; familiar.
Personal; private.
A very close friend.
Women's underwear, sleepwear, or lingerie, especially offered for sale in a store.
To suggest or disclose (something) discreetly.
To notify.

intimate.ety: Borrowed from Latin intimātus, the perfect passive participle of intimō (“to put or bring into, to impress, to make familiar”) (see -ate (adjective forming suffix)), from intimus (“inmost, innermost, most intimate”), superlative of intus (“within”), from in (“in”); see interior.

ex.en: The two boys became intimate friends at the camp.
ex.ja: ２人の少年はキャンプで親しい友達になった。

ex.en: This party is an intimate gathering.
ex.ja: このパーティーは親しい人の集まりです。

ex.en: My acquaintance introduced me to his intimate fellows.
ex.ja: 私の知人が私を彼の親しい友人達に紹介した。

note.ja: ラテン語 intimus（最も内側の）から。→「親密な・個人的な・ほのめかす」。

en: A laundering; a washing.
A place or room where laundering is done - including, by extension, other forms of laundering than clothes washing.

laundry.ety: From Middle English lavendrie, from Old French lavanderie, from Latin lavandaria. See launder.

ex.en: May I wash all my laundry at once?
ex.ja: まとめて洗濯していいですか。

ex.en: If the laundry is dry, bring it in.
ex.ja: 洗濯物乾いてたら取り込んで。

ex.en: Thank you for doing the laundry for me.
ex.ja: 洗濯してくれてるんだ。ありがとう。

note.ja: ラテン語 lavare（洗う）から。lavatory（洗面所）と同じ。→「洗濯物・洗濯・クリーニング店」。

en: Of, relating to, or suggestive of war; warlike.
Connected with or relating to armed forces or the profession of arms or military life.

martial.ety: From Middle English martial, marcial, mercial, mercialle (“relating to war, warlike; military; for use in fighting or warfare; brave, hardy; combative, fierce; ruthless, vicious; domineering, overbearing”), from Middle French martial (modern French martial (“martial”)), or directly from its etymon Latin mārtiālis (“of or pertaining to Mars, the Roman god of war”), from Mārtius (“of or pertaining to Mars”) + -ālis (suffix forming adjectives of relationship). The English word is cognate with Italian marziale (“martial”), Portuguese marcial (“martial”), Spanish marcial (“martial”).

ex.en: Our teacher is a martial arts expert.
ex.ja: 先生は武道の達人です。

ex.en: Tom is a martial artist.

en: Capable of reasoning.

ex.ja: これには合理的な説明が必要だ。

en: A sphere of knowledge or of influence; a domain.

ex.ja: 言語を学ぶには曖昧さに対する寛容性が必要である。

en: A line segment joining the vertex of triangle to the midpoint of the opposing side.
A number separating the higher half from the lower half of a data sample, population, or probability distribution. The median of a finite…
Situated in a middle, central, or intermediate part, section, or range of (something).
In the middle of an organ, structure etc.; towards the median plane of an organ or limb.

median.ety: Borrowed from Middle French median, from Latin mediānus (“of or pertaining to the middle”, adjective), from medius (“middle”) (see medium), from Proto-Indo-European *médʰyos (“middle”). Doublet of mean and mizzen. Cognate with Old English midde, middel (“middle”). More at middle.

ex.en: The median age of the town's people is forty.
ex.ja: その町の住民の年齢の中央値は４０歳だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 medianus（中間の）から。medius。「中央値」。medium、middle と同じ。

en: Of or relating to the Middle Ages, the period from approximately 500 to 1500 AD.
Archaic.
Someone living in the Middle Ages.
A medieval example (of something aforementioned or understood from context).

medieval.ety: From French médiéval (“medieval”), from Latin medium (“middle”) + aevum (“age”).

ex.en: My major is medieval European history.
ex.ja: 私の専門は中世ヨーロッパ史です。

ex.en: I was deeply impressed with the medieval music.
ex.ja: 私はその中世の音楽に深い感銘を受けた。

ex.en: The medieval times were an age when a human being wasn't free.
ex.ja: 中世は人間が自由でない時代だった。

note.ja: ラテン語 medium aevum（中間の時代）から。→「中世の」。

en: The ability to move; capacity for movement.
A tendency to sudden change; mutability, changeableness.

mobility.ety: From Middle French mobilité, and its source, Latin mōbilitās (“mobility”).

ex.en: Elevators improve mobility for elderly people.
ex.ja: エレベーターはお年寄りの移動を楽にする。

note.ja: ラテン語 mobilitas から。mobilis（動かせる）、movere（動かす）。「移動のしやすさ」。mobile と同じ。

en: A chamber used for baking or heating.
A very hot place.
To cook in an oven.

en: An official document normally used for international journeys, which proves the identity and nationality of the person for whom it was is…
Any document that allows entry or passage.
To regulate how money given to a local authority must be spent.
Providing the legal requirements to enable or legitimize cross-border economic activity.

passport.ety: From French passeport, from passer (“pass”) + port (“port”). Compare portpass. Equivalent to pass + port.

ex.en: Would you mind letting me see your passport?
ex.ja: パスポートを拝見できますか。

ex.en: If I find your passport, I'll call you.
ex.ja: 君のパスポート見つけたら、電話するね。

ex.en: Oh, no! I may have lost my passport.
ex.ja: やばい、パスポートなくしたかも。

note.ja: pass（通る）+ port（港）。港を通る許可 →「旅券・パスポート」。

Of a woven fabric surface, to form small matted balls of fiber.

ex.ja: 医者達は私に睡眠薬しか出してくれなかった。

ex.ja: この薬を飲めば、気分が良くなりますよ。

ex.en: I have to take two pills every six hours.
ex.ja: 私は６時間ごとに２粒飲まなければなりません。

note.ja: ラテン語 pilula（小さな玉）から。pila（玉）。「錠剤」。pellet と同系。

en: A mammal of most genera of the family Leporidae, with long ears, long hind legs and a short, fluffy tail. (Those of the larger kind are i…
The meat from this animal.
To hunt rabbits.
To flee.

rabbit.ety:
Inherited from Middle English rabet, rabette, from Anglo-Latin rabettus, from dialectal Old French rabotte, probably a diminutive of Middle Dutch or West Flemish robbe (“rabbit, seal”), of uncertain origin; possibly some imitative verb, maybe robben, rubben (“to rub”) is used here to allude to a characteristic of the animal. See rub.
Related forms include Middle French rabouillet (“baby rabbit”) and in French rabot (“plane”)), coming via Walloon Old French (reflected nowadays as Walloon robète (“rabbit”)), from Middle Dutch robbe ("rabbit; seal"; whence Modern Dutch rob (“rabbit", also "seal”)

ex.en: "What's the matter?" asked the little white rabbit.
ex.ja: 「どうかしたの？」と小さな白いウサギが聞きました。

ex.en: A lot of boys ran after the rabbit.
ex.ja: たくさんの少年達がそのウサギを追いかけた。

ex.en: "Forever and always?" asked the little black rabbit.
ex.ja: 「いつも、そしていつまでも？」と小さい黒いウサギはききました。

note.ja: 中英語 rabet から。古フランス語の方言に由来するとされる。hare は野ウサギ。

en: The variation of strong and weak elements (such as duration, accent) of sounds, notably in speech or music, over time; a beat or meter.
A specifically defined pattern of such variation.
To impart a (particular) rhythm to.

ex.ja: あの歌のゆっくりしたリズムが好きです。

ex.en: You have no sense of rhythm.
ex.ja: リズム感ないわね。

ex.en: Samba is a Brazilian rhythm, isn't it?
ex.ja: サンバはブラジルのリズムですね。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 rhythmos（流れ・拍子）から。→「リズム・律動」。

en: Wild; not cultivated or tamed.
Barbaric; not civilized.
An aggressively defiant person.
To attack or assault someone or something ferociously or without restraint.
To criticise vehemently.

savage.ety: From Middle English savage, from Old French sauvage, salvage (“wild, untamed”), from Late Latin salvāticus, alteration of Latin silvāticus (“wild”, literally “of the woods”), from silva (“forest; grove”). Doublet of sylvatic.

ex.en: The savage in man is never quite eradicated.
ex.ja: 人間の野蛮性は決して根絶できない。

ex.en: He is quite a savage.
ex.ja: 彼は全くの野蛮人だ。

ex.en: There are still some savage tribes on that island.
ex.ja: その島には未開種族がいる。

note.ja: ラテン語 silvaticus（森の）から。silva（森）。「森に住む」→「野蛮な・どう猛な」。

en: Someone who shoots something; a gunner, archer, etc.
The player throwing the dice.

shooter.ety: From Middle English schoter, schuter, schotter, scheter, schetare, scheotere, from Old English sċēotere (“shooter”), equivalent to shoot + -er. Compare Dutch schieter, schutter (“shooter”), German Schießer (“shooter”), Swedish skjutare, West Frisian sjitter (“shooter”).

ex.en: He is a square shooter.
ex.ja: 彼は正直者だ。

note.ja: shoot（撃つ）+ -er。「射手」。

en: A person who shares a parent; one's brother or sister who one shares a parent with.
A node in a data structure that shares its parent with another node.

sibling.ety: First use appears c. 1903, a modern revival of Old English sibling (“relative, a relation, kinsman”), equivalent to sib + -ling. Compare Middle English siblynges pl, sib, sibbe (“relative; kinsman”), German Sippe. The term apparently meant merely kin or relative until the 20th century when it was applied in a way that aided the study of genetics, which led to its specialized use. For example, the OED has a citation in 1902 in which sibling must be defined for those who do not know the intended meaning.

ex.en: She works as hard as her siblings.
ex.ja: 彼女は兄弟たちと同じくらい一生懸命に働く。

ex.en: "Do you have any siblings?" "No, I'm an only child."
ex.ja: 「兄弟はいますか？」「いいえ、一人っ子です」

ex.en: How many siblings do you have?
ex.ja: きょうだいは何人ですか。

note.ja: 古英語 sibb（親族）+ ling（小さな者）。→「兄弟姉妹（性別を問わない言い方）」。

en: Slender in an attractive way.
Designed to make the wearer appear slim.
A type of cigarette substantially longer and thinner than normal cigarettes.
A potato farl.
To lose weight in order to achieve slimness.
To make slimmer; to reduce in size.

slim.ety:
Borrowing from Low German or Dutch slim (“bad, sly, clever”), from Middle Dutch slim (“bad, crooked”), from Old Dutch *slimb, from Proto-West Germanic *slimb, from Proto-Germanic *slimbaz (“oblique, crooked”). The sense development would have been "slanting, cunning" (Dutch) > "insignificant, slight" and then "thin, graceful" in English, a shift that Liberman calls an "incredible amelioration" of word meaning.
The pejorative sense found in Low German and Dutch is also found preserved in the archaic English noun slim (“worthless or lazy person”), also comparable to the South African use of the

ex.en: Young girls' desire for slim figures is strong.
ex.ja: ほっそりとした姿に対する若い女性の願望は強い。

ex.en: Chances of promotion are slim in this firm.
ex.ja: この会社では昇進の見込みがない。

ex.en: Both young and old people desire slim figures.
ex.ja: 若人も老人も、ほっそりとした姿を望む。

note.ja: オランダ語 slim（悪い・ずるい）から意味が変化。→「ほっそりした・（可能性が）わずかな」。

en: Sometime; at some unspecified time in the future.

ex.en: Someday the new research work will be completed.
ex.ja: その新しい研究はいつか完成するだろう。

ex.en: I would like to visit New York someday.
ex.ja: いつかニューヨークに行ってみたいものだ。

ex.en: I'm sure he's going to be somebody someday.
ex.ja: 彼は今にひとかどの人物になるよ。

note.ja: some + day。「いつか（未来の日）」。

en: Of a person: having obtained worldly experience, and lacking naiveté; cosmopolitan, worldly-wise.
Of art or other things: appealing to the tastes of an intellectual or sophisticated (sense 1) person; cerebral; also, cultured, elegant, …

sophisticated.ety: First English usage circa 1601. From Medieval Latin sophisticatus.

ex.en: The readers of that book think themselves sophisticated.
ex.ja: あの本の読者たちは自分のことをインテリだと思っている。

ex.en: Modern finance is becoming increasingly complicated and sophisticated.
ex.ja: 現代の金融は一段と複雑かつ高度になってきている。

ex.en: He looks quite sophisticated for his age.
ex.ja: 彼は年の割にとても世慣れて見える。

note.ja: ギリシャ語 sophistēs（賢者・詭弁家）から。soph（知恵）。手を加えすぎた →「洗練された・精巧な」。

en: A large quantity or multitude of anything done repetitively or considered unusually or indiscriminately repetitive.
A type of tinned meat made mainly from ham.
To do something rapidly and repeatedly.

spam.ety:
The original sense (canned ham) is a proprietary name registered by Geo. A. Hormel & Co. in U.S., 1937. It is presumed to be a conflation of either "spiced ham" or "shoulder of pork and ham" but was soon extended to other kinds of canned meat. Hormel spells the trademarked name in all upper case.
The use for unsolicited and unwanted email derives from a Monty Python's Flying Circus sketch. In the 1970 sketch, a group of Vikings in a restaurant repeatedly chant the word "spam". The earliest recorded real-life use for this sense occurs around 1993 which finds reference in a newsgroup post dated

ex.ja: うっとうしい、また迷惑メール来てる。

ex.en: Another spam article hoping for click-throughs?
ex.ja: またアフィ狙いの記事か。

ex.en: Look in your spam folder.
ex.ja: スパムフォルダを確認してみて。

note.ja: 缶詰肉の商標 SPAM を連呼するコメディの場面から →「迷惑メール」。

en: A large pile of hay, grain, straw, or the like, larger at the bottom than the top, sometimes covered with thatch.
A pile of similar objects, each directly on top of the last.
To arrange in a stack, or to add to an existing stack.
To arrange the cards in a deck in a particular manner, especially for cheating.

stack.ety:
From Middle English stack, stacke, stakke, stak, from Old Norse stakkr (“a barn; haystack; heap; pile”), from Proto-Germanic *stakkaz (“a barn; rick; haystack”).
The data structure sense is a calque of Dutch stapel, introduced by Edsger W. Dijkstra. Cognate with Icelandic stakkur (“stack”), Swedish stack (“stack”), Danish stak (“stack”), Norwegian stakk (“stack”). Related to stake and sauna.

ex.en: Only one stack had a real bill on top.
ex.ja: 一束だけ一番上に本物の札がのっていた。

ex.en: There is a stack of letters on the table.
ex.ja: テーブルの上に手紙が山積みになっている。

ex.en: If you stack the dishes up by the sink, I'll do them later.
ex.ja: 流しの横にお皿を積んでおいてくだされば、後で私が洗います。

note.ja: 古北欧語 stakkr（干し草の山）から。「積み重ね」。

en: The manner, pose, or posture in which one stands.
One's opinion or point of view.
To place, to position, to station; (specifically) to put (cattle) into an enclosure or pen in preparation for sale.

stance.ety:
From Middle English staunce (“place to stand; battle station; position; standing in society; circumstance, situation; stanchion”), from Old French estance (“predicament; situation; sojourn, stay”) (compare modern French stance (“stanza; position one stands in when golfing”)), from Italian stanza (“room, standing place; stanza”), from Vulgar Latin *stantia, from Latin stō (“to stand; to remain, stay”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *steh₂- (“to stand (up)”). The word is cognate with Spanish estante (“shelf”) and a doublet of stanza.
The verb is derived from the noun.
Compare typologically

ex.ja: この構えはホームラン狙ってるな。

ex.en: He took an uncertain stance.
ex.ja: 彼はあいまいな態度をとった。

ex.en: Western countries are jumping on Japan for its stance on the issue.
ex.ja: 西欧諸国はこの問題に対する日本の姿勢を激しく非難しています。

note.ja: ラテン語 stare（立つ）から。stan + ce。立ち方 →「姿勢・立場」。

Interference on a broadcast signal caused by atmospheric disturbances; heard as crackles on radio, or seen as random specks on television.
Interference or obstruction from people.

en: An underground railway, especially for mass transit of people in urban areas.
A train that runs on such an underground railway.
To travel by underground railway.

ex.ja: 一人で地下鉄に乗るのは危ないですか。

ex.en: What subway goes to the center of town?
ex.ja: どの地下鉄が町の中心部へ行きますか。

ex.ja: 彼女はバスから地下鉄に乗り換えた。

en: A slab of clay, stone or wood used for inscription.
A short scripture written by the founders of the Baháʼí Faith.
To form (a drug, etc.) into tablets.

tablet.ety: From Middle English tablet, from Old French tablete (Modern French tablette), diminutive of table (“table”). Compare English table, -et.

ex.ja: ラベルには１回２錠と書いてある。

ex.en: This tablet isn't doing what it's supposed to do.
ex.ja: このタブレット、言うこと聞いてくれないんです。

ex.ja: 錠剤のおかげで痛みがなくなった。

To go camping.
To prop up aluminum foil in an inverted "V" (reminiscent of a pop-up tent) over food to reduce splatter, before putting it in the oven.

ex.ja: テントの中ではなくて外で食べよう。

ex.en: Let's pitch the tent while it's still light.
ex.ja: 明るい内にテントを張ってしまおう。

deploy.ety: Borrowed from French déployer (“to unroll, unfold”), from Old French desploiier, itself from des- + ploiier, or possibly from Late Latin displicāre (“to unfold, display”), from Latin dis- (“apart”) + plicare (“to fold”). Compare Middle English desployen, dysployen (“to unfold, display”). Doublet of display.

ex.en: The government deployed troops to the border.
ex.ja: 政府は国境に部隊を配備した。

note.ja: de（= dis 離れて）+ ploy（折る）。折りたたんだものを広げる →「（部隊を）配備する・展開する」。

en: Not to have the same traits or characteristics; to be unalike or distinct.
To be separated in quantity.
A program that diffs, a diff.

en: Desirous; keen to do or obtain something.
Not employing lazy evaluation; calculating results immediately, rather than deferring calculation until they are required.
To be or become eager.
To express eagerness.

Inherited from Middle English egre, eger, from Old French aigre, egre (modern French aigre), from Latin ācrus, variant of ācer (“sharp, keen”); see acid, acerb, etc. Compare vinegar, alegar.

ex.en: Tom is eager to buy a new car.
ex.ja: トムはしきりに新車を買いたがっている。

ex.en: We are all eager to know the truth.
ex.ja: 私たちはみな真実を知りたがっています。

ex.en: We are all eager to see the movie.
ex.ja: 私達はみな、その映画を見たいと熱望しています。

note.ja: 古フランス語 aigre（鋭い）から。ラテン語 acer。「鋭い」→「熱心な」。acid と同系。

en: Raised, usually above ground level.
Increased, particularly above a normal level.
An elevated railway.

ex.en: The doctor said my blood pressure was elevated.
ex.ja: 医師は私の血圧が高いと言った。

note.ja: elevate（持ち上げる）+ -ed。「高い・高架の」。

en: The inherent nature of a thing or idea.
The true nature of anything, not accidental or illusory.

essence.ety: From Middle English essence, from Middle French essence, from Latin essentia (“the being or essence of a thing”), from an artificial formation of esse (“to be”), to translate Ancient Greek οὐσία (ousía, “being”), from ὤν (ṓn), present participle of εἰμί (eimí, “to be, exist”). Displaced native Old English understandennes (literally, "understanden-ness").

ex.en: Freedom is the very essence of our democracy.
ex.ja: 自由こそまさに我々の民主主義の神髄だ。

ex.en: This, in essence, is the secret of science.
ex.ja: 実はこれこそが科学の神髄なのである。

ex.en: Human history is in essence a history of ideas.
ex.ja: 人間の歴史は本質的には思想の歴史である。

note.ja: ラテン語 esse（ある・存在する）から。「そのものが“ある”ための中身」→「本質」。抽出した中身 →「エッセンス」。essential（不可欠な）。

en: The hairy coat of various mammal species, especially when fine, soft and thick.
The hairy skins of animals used as a material for clothing.
To cover with fur or a fur-like coating.
To become covered with fur or a fur-like coating.

fur.ety:

From Middle English furre, forre, from Anglo-Norman forre, fuerre (“case; sheath”), from Frankish *fōdar, from Proto-West Germanic *fōdr, from Proto-Germanic *fōdrą (“sheath”) (compare Old English fōdor (“sheaf”), Dutch voering (“lining”), German Futter (“lining”), Gothic 𐍆𐍉𐌳𐍂 (fōdr, “sheath”)), from Proto-Indo-European *peh₂-, *poh₂- (“to protect”) (compare Lithuanian piemuō (“protection”), Ancient Greek πῶῠ̈ (pôŭ̈, “flock”), πῶμα (pôma, “lid”), ποιμή

ex.en: She had to part with her fur coat.
ex.ja: 彼女は毛皮のコートを手放さなければならなかった。

ex.en: His body was covered with brown fur.
ex.ja: 体は茶色の毛をしていた。

ex.en: Her coat is fur on the inside.
ex.ja: 彼女のコートの内側は毛皮になっている。

note.ja: 古フランス語 forrer（裏打ちする）から。「毛皮の裏地」→「毛皮」。

en: The process of gathering the ripened crop; harvesting.
The yield of harvesting, i.e., the gathered crops or fruits.
To bring in a harvest; reap; glean.
To take a living organism as part of a managed process to gather food or resources, often with the intention of maintaining a healthy pop…

harvest.ety:
From Middle English harvest, hervest, from Old English hærfest (“autumn, harvest-time; August”), from Proto-West Germanic *harbist, from Proto-Germanic *harbistaz (“harvest-time, autumn, fall”), from *harbaz, from Proto-Indo-European *kerp-.
Cognates
Cognate with Sylt North Frisian Hārefst, West Frisian hjerst, Dutch herfst, German Herbst, dated German Low German Harvst, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål høst, Norwegian Nynorsk haust; further with Latin carpere (“to seize”), Ancient Greek καρπός (karpós, “fruit”), κείρω (keírō, “to cut off”).

ex.en: A festival is held at the rice harvest.
ex.ja: 稲の収穫期にはお祭りをする。

ex.en: We thought we might expect a good harvest.
ex.ja: 相当な収穫を期待してもよいと思った。

ex.en: This year's harvest will fall short of last year.
ex.ja: 今年の収穫は昨年に及ばないだろう。

note.ja: 古英語で「秋」を意味した語。秋は刈り入れの季節 →「収穫」。

en: A rope or chain used to attach the bow of a vessel to the shore or to another vessel.
A rope tied to the head of an animal.
To give a headline to a page or section of a text.
To present as the main attraction; to have top billing, to be the main attraction.

ex.en: The actor's death made big headlines in all the papers.
ex.ja: その俳優の死は各紙で大見出しで報じられた。

note.ja: head（頭）+ line（行）。「頭の行」→「見出し」→「主役を務める」。

To promote or advertise heavily.
Hyped; excited.

en: Miscellaneous items of little value, especially discarded or unwanted items.
Material or resources of poor quality or low value, especially resources that lack commercial value.
To throw away.
To find something for very little money (meaning derived from the term junkshop)

junk.ety: From earlier meaning "old refuse from boats and ships", from Middle English junk, jounke, jonk, joynk (“an old cable or rope”, nautical term), sometimes cut into bits and used as caulking; of uncertain origin; perhaps related to join, joint, juncture. Often compared to Middle English junk, jonk, jonke, junck (“a rush; basket made of rushes”), from Old French jonc, from Latin iuncus (“rush, reed”); however, the Oxford English Dictionary finds "no evidence of connexion".

ex.en: All this junk needs to be thrown away.
ex.ja: このゴミ、全部捨てなきゃ。

ex.en: This car is no better than junk.
ex.ja: この車はがらくた同然である。

ex.en: Tom used to eat a lot of junk food.
ex.ja: トムは以前はジャンクフードをたくさん食べていた。

note.ja: 中英語 jonke（古い綱）から。「古いくず」→「がらくた」。中国の帆船の junk は別語。

en: An organ in the body that filters the blood, producing urine.
This organ (of an animal) cooked as food.

kidney.ety: From Middle English kideney, kydeney, alteration of earlier kidenere (“kidney”) after ey (“egg”), of obscure origin and formation. The first element would be from Old English *cydde (“sack, scrotum”), from Proto-Germanic *kuddijā (“sack”), as the terms for testicle and kidney were often interchangeable in Germanic (compare Old High German nioro (“kidney", also "testicle”), Old Swedish vig-niauri (“testicle”)); the second is from Old English *nēora or Middle Low German nêre (“kidney”), from Proto-

ex.en: I have kidney trouble.
ex.ja: 腎臓が悪いのです。

ex.en: Tom's kidneys and liver are in bad shape.
ex.ja: トムは腎臓と肝臓が悪い。

note.ja: 中英語 kidenei から。語源ははっきりしない。「腎臓」。

en: A frame, usually portable, of wood, metal, or rope, used for ascent and descent, consisting of two side pieces to which are fastened rung…
A series of stages by which one progresses to a better position.
To arrange or form into a shape of a ladder.
To ascend (a building, a wall, etc.) using a ladder.

ladder.ety:
Inherited from Middle English ladder, laddre; from Old English hlǣder, from Proto-West Germanic *hlaidriju, from Proto-Germanic *hlaidrijō, from Proto-Indo-European *ḱlóydʰrom, from *ḱley- (“to lean”).
Compare Scots ledder, North Frisian ladder, Saterland Frisian Laadere, West Frisian ljedder, Dutch ladder, German Leiter; also Old Irish clithar (“hedge”), and Umbrian 𐌊𐌋𐌄𐌈𐌓𐌀𐌌 (kleθram, “stretcher”). See lean, which is related to lid.
Further cognates include Ashkun istrī, Kamkata-viri c̣ik, Prasuni čik, čix; Waigali c̣iř, Sanskrit श्रिति (śrití).

ex.en: My father put a ladder against the tree.
ex.ja: 父は木にはしごを立てかけた。

ex.en: Is this ladder strong enough to bear my weight?
ex.ja: このはしごはわたしの体重を支えるのに十分なほど丈夫なのですか。

ex.en: He put his foot on the ladder.
ex.ja: 彼ははしごに片足を掛けた。

note.ja: 古英語 hlǣder から。lean（傾く）と同系で「立てかけるもの」。

en: An entryway or reception area; vestibule; passageway; corridor.
That part of a hall of legislation not appropriated to the official use of the assembly.
To attempt to influence (a public official or decision-maker) in favor of a specific opinion or cause.

ex.ja: トムがロビーで待ってるよ。

en: Any naturally occurring solid material that has a (more or less) definite chemical composition and characteristic physical properties; es…
Any inorganic material (as distinguished from animal or vegetable).
of, related to, or containing minerals

mineral.ety: From Middle English mineral, borrowed from Old French mineral, (French minéral), from Medieval Latin minerale, from minera (“ore”), probably ultimately derived from Latin mina (“ore, mine”).

ex.en: The region is relatively rich in mineral resources.
ex.ja: その地域は鉱物資源が比較的豊かだ。

ex.en: The province is relatively rich in mineral resources.
ex.ja: その州は鉱物資源が比較的豊富だ。

ex.en: That country is rich in mineral resources.
ex.ja: その国は鉱物資源に恵まれている。

note.ja: ラテン語 minera（鉱山）から。mine（鉱山・掘る）と同じ。「鉱山から掘り出すもの」→「鉱物・ミネラル」。

en: A large or disorderly group of people; especially one bent on riotous or destructive action.
A group of animals of any kind.
To crowd around (someone), sometimes with hostility.
To crowd into or around a place.

mob.ety: From Middle English mob, short for mobile, from Latin mōbile (vulgus) (“fickle (crowd)”).

ex.en: He battled his way out of the mob.
ex.ja: 彼は群衆の中から必死になって抜け出した。

ex.en: The policeman was confronted by the angry mob.
ex.ja: その警察官は怒っている群集と向かい合った。

ex.en: The mob gathered round the car like so many flies.
ex.ja: 群衆がまるでハエのようにその車の周りに集まった。

note.ja: ラテン語 mobile vulgus（気まぐれな群衆）の短縮。「暴徒・群衆」。mobile と同じ。

en: Not bragging or boasting about oneself or one's achievements; unpretentious, humble.
Small, moderate in size.

modest.ety: From Middle French modeste, from Latin modestus.

ex.en: The union was modest in its wage demands.
ex.ja: その組合の賃上げ要求は穏当だった。

ex.en: How can I say things to sound modest?
ex.ja: どう言えば、おしとやかに聞こえる？

ex.en: There was a modest rise in prices last year.
ex.ja: 昨年の物価上昇はまあまあだった。

note.ja: ラテン語 modus（尺度・ほどよさ）から。「度を越さない」→「控えめな・謙虚な」。mode（方式）、moderate（適度な）も同じ。

en: The theory, practice and technology of charting a course for a road vehicle, ship, aircraft, or spaceship.
Traffic or travel by vessel, especially commercial shipping.

navigation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French navigation, from Latin nāvigātiōnem, accusative singular of nāvigātiō (“sailing, navigation”), from nāvigō (“sail”). Morphologically navigate + -ion.

ex.en: Early explorers used the stars for navigation.
ex.ja: 昔の探検家たちは航海するのに星を利用した。

ex.en: He has a superficial knowledge of navigation.
ex.ja: 彼は航海については表面的な知識しか持っていない。

ex.en: The harbor is closed to navigation.
ex.ja: その港は船の航行が止められている。

note.ja: nav（船）+ igat（動かす）+ ion。船を進めること →「航海・航行・道案内」。

en: An elliptical movement of an object about a celestial object or Lagrange point, especially a periodic elliptical revolution.
One complete circuit round an orbited body.
To circle or revolve around another object or position.
To place an object (e.g. a satellite) into an orbit around a planet.

orbit.ety:
Etymology tree

Latin orbitabor.
Middle English orbita
Middle English orbite
English orbit
Inherited from Middle English orbite, orbita, from Latin orbita (“course, track, impression, mark”).

ex.en: The satellite is in orbit around the moon.
ex.ja: 衛星は月の周りの軌道に乗っている。

ex.en: The rocket is in orbit around the moon.
ex.ja: ロケットは月を回る軌道に乗っている。

ex.en: The spaceship is out of orbit around the moon.
ex.ja: 宇宙船は月を回る軌道を外れている。

note.ja: ラテン語 orbis（輪・円）から。「輪を描く道」→「軌道」。

en: A passage in text that starts on a new line, the first line sometimes being indented, and usually marks a change of topic.
A mark or note set in the margin to call attention to something in the text, such as a change of subject.
To sort text into paragraphs.
To publish a brief article, notice, or announcement, as in a newspaper.

paragraph.ety: From Middle English paragraf, from Middle French paragraphe from Latin paragraphus (“sign for start of a new section of discourse”), from Ancient Greek παράγραφος (parágraphos), from παρά (pará, “beside”) and γράφω (gráphō, “to write”). Doublet of paragraphos.

ex.en: Can you understand the meaning of this paragraph?
ex.ja: この段落の意味分かる？

ex.en: Start a new paragraph here.
ex.ja: ここで改行しなさい。

ex.en: Please refer to paragraph ten.
ex.ja: １０項を参照して下さい。

note.ja: para（そばに）+ graph（書く）。（区切りを示すために）横に書いた印 →「段落」。

en: Being subjected to an action without producing a reaction.
Taking no action.
The passive voice of verbs.
A form of a verb that is in the passive voice.

passive.ety: From Middle English passyf, passyve, from Middle French, French passif, from Latin passivus (“serving to express the suffering of an action; in late Latin literally capable of suffering or feeling”), from passus, past participle of pati (“to suffer”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *peh₁- (“to hurt”); compare patient.

ex.en: Watching TV is a passive activity.
ex.ja: テレビを見ることは受動的活動である。

ex.en: He is passive in everything.
ex.ja: 彼は何をするにも消極的だ。

ex.en: He has a passive character.
ex.ja: 彼は消極的な性格だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 pati（受ける・苦しむ）から。pass + ive。受け身の →「消極的な・受動的な」。

en: A piece of land projecting into water from a larger land mass.

peninsula.ety: Borrowed from Latin paenīnsula, from paene (“almost”), and īnsula (“island”).

ex.en: Have you ever been to the Korean Peninsula?
ex.ja: 朝鮮半島を訪れたことがありますか。

ex.en: A humid climate is characteristic of the peninsula.
ex.ja: 湿気の多い気候はその半島の特色です。

note.ja: pen（ほとんど）+ insula（島）。「ほとんど島」→「半島」。insulate（隔離する・島にする）、isolate も同じ insula から。

en: The meat of a pig.

Proto-Italic *porkos

ex.ja: 僕はクリスチャンだけど、豚肉は食べない。

ex.en: I am Christian but I don't eat pork.
ex.ja: 私はクリスチャンですけど、豚肉は食べません。

ex.en: As for me, I like chicken better than pork.
ex.ja: 私について言えば、豚肉より鶏肉のほうが好きです。

zh: 葡萄牙語的 /葡萄牙语的

en: Of or pertaining to Portugal.
Of or pertaining to the people of Portugal or their culture.
A person native to, or living in, Portugal.

Portuguese.ety: From Portuguese português. By surface analysis, Portugal + -ese.

ex.en: I'm looking for someone who can speak Portuguese.
ex.ja: ポルトガル語のできる人を探しています。

ex.en: No other language is as beautiful as Portuguese.
ex.ja: ポルトガル語ほど美しい言語はない。

ex.en: I can't even speak Portuguese, let alone English.
ex.ja: 私はポルトガル語なんて話せないし、まして英語なんて。

note.ja: Portugal は港町 Porto（港）の古名 Portus Cale から。port（港）と同じ語源。

en: Producing a profit.
Beneficial, serviceable, of use.

profitable.ety: From Old French profitable, equivalent to profit + -able.

ex.en: What you've done is profitable only to the enemy.
ex.ja: 君がやったことは利敵行為だ。

ex.en: The opinions were divided on which one is profitable.
ex.ja: どちらが得かは、意見が分かれるとこだ。

ex.en: This job is not profitable.
ex.ja: この仕事は割に合わない。

note.ja: profit（利益）+ -able。profit は pro（前へ）+ facere（作る）。「前に進ませるもの」→「利益」。

en: A large plot of land used for raising cattle, sheep or other livestock.
A small farm that cultivates vegetables or livestock, especially one in the Southwestern United States.
To operate a ranch; to engage in ranching.
To work on a ranch.

ranch.ety: Recorded since 1808, farm sense since 1831. From American Spanish rancho (“small farm, group of farm huts”), in Spanish originally “group of people who eat together." Cognate with English rank.

ex.en: His ranch covers twenty square miles.
ex.ja: 彼の牧場は、２０平方マイルに及んでいる。

ex.en: There are about 500 cattle on the ranch.
ex.ja: その牧場には牛が５００頭ばかりいる。

ex.en: What is the acreage of your ranch?
ex.ja: あなたの牧場は何エーカーありますか。

note.ja: スペイン語 rancho（小屋・食事の集まり）から。「大牧場」。

en: In accordance with reason.
Fairly; satisfactorily; not extremely.

reasonably.ety: From Middle English resonably, equivalent to reasonable + -ly. Piecewise doublet of rationably.

ex.en: You can reasonably expect her to come.
ex.ja: 彼女は来るものと君が考えるのはもっともなことだ。

ex.en: We can not reasonably ask more.
ex.ja: これ以上求められないのは当然だ。

ex.en: How long does it take to get reasonably skilled?
ex.ja: そこそこ腕が立つようになるにはどれくらいの時間がかかるものでしょうか？

note.ja: reasonable + -ly。「理にかなって」→「かなり・ほどほどに」。

en: A part or parts remaining after some has/have been removed or already occurred.
The amount left over after subtracting the divisor as many times as possible from the dividend without producing a negative result. If n …
Remaining.
To mark or declare items left unsold as subject to reduction in price.

remainder.ety: From Middle English remaindre, remeigner, from Anglo-Norman remaindre, with infinitive used as noun.

ex.en: Find the remainder when 2²⁰¹³ is divided by 3.
ex.ja: 2²⁰¹³を3で割った余りを求めよ。

ex.en: He was excused from the remainder of the work.
ex.ja: 彼は残りの仕事を免除された。

note.ja: re（後ろに）+ main（とどまる）+ der。後に残っているもの →「残り」。remain（残る）。

en: To deliberately take hold of; to grab or capture.
To take advantage of (an opportunity or circumstance).

seize.ety: Earlier seise, from Middle English seisen, sesen, saisen, from Old French seisir (“to take possession of; invest (person, court)”), from Early Medieval Latin sacīre (“to lay claim to, appropriate”) (8th century) in the phrase ad propriam sacire, from Old Low Frankish *sakjan (“to sue, bring legal action”), from Proto-Germanic *sakjaną, *sakōną (compare Old English sacian (“to strive, brawl”)), from Proto-Germanic *sakaną (compare Old Saxon sakan (“to accuse”), Old High German sahhan (“to bicker, quarrel, rebuke”), Old English sacan (“to quarrel, claim by law, accuse”). Cognate to sake and Lati

ex.en: I seized the cat by the neck.
ex.ja: 私は猫の首筋をつかんだ。

ex.en: The man seized him by the neck.
ex.ja: 男は彼のえり首をつかんだ。

ex.en: He seized the boy by the arm.
ex.ja: 彼は少年の腕をつかんだ。

note.ja: 古フランス語 seisir（所有権を得る）から。「ぐっとつかんで自分のものにする」→「つかむ・押収する」。seizure（押収・発作）。

en: Half of a school year (US) or academic year such as autumn or spring semester.
A period or term of six months.

semester.ety: From German Semester, from New Latin sēmestris (“lasting six months”), from sex (“six”) + mēnsis (“month”).

ex.en: What are you going to take this semester?
ex.ja: 今学期はどんな教科を選択しますか。

ex.en: In Japan, the new semester begins in April.
ex.ja: 日本では新学期は４月から始まる。

ex.en: I haven't studied physics much all semester.
ex.ja: 私は今学期物理をあまり勉強しなかった。

note.ja: ラテン語 sex（6）+ mensis（月）。「6か月」→「（半年単位の）学期」。

en: A general thought, feeling, or sense.
Feelings, especially tender feelings, as apart from reason or judgment, or of a weak or foolish kind.

sentiment.ety:

Proto-Italic *sentiō

Proto-Indo-European *-mn̥tom

English sentiment
From Old French sentement, from Latin sentimentum.

ex.en: Mary is a girl full of sentiment.
ex.ja: メアリーは気持ちのやさしい女の子だ。

ex.en: She is a girl full of sentiment.
ex.ja: 彼女は気持ちのやさしい女の子だ。

ex.en: She expressed her sentiments on the war.
ex.ja: 彼女は戦争について所感を述べた。

note.ja: ラテン語 sentire（感じる）から。「感じたこと」→「感情・意見」。sense、sensitive、consent（同意する）も同じ。

en: A knitted or woven covering for the foot.
Synonym of soccus, a light shoe worn by Ancient Greek and Roman comedic actors.
The sound of a punch or powerful blow.

sock.ety: From Middle English socke, sokke, sok, from Old English socc (“sock, light shoe, slipper”), a West Germanic borrowing from Latin soccus (“a light shoe or slipper, buskin”), from Ancient Greek σύκχος (súkkhos, “a kind of shoe”), probably from Phrygian or from an Anatolian language. Beekes compares Avestan 𐬵𐬀𐬑𐬀 (haxa, “sole of the foot”). Cognate with Scots sok (“sock, stocking”), West Frisian sok (“sock”), Dutch sok (“sock”), German Socke (“sock”), Danish sok, sokke (“sock”), Swedish sock, socka (“sock”), Icelandic sokkur (“sock”). Doublet of zocco; also related to zoccolo, socle, and zocalo.

ex.en: You are wearing your socks inside out.
ex.ja: 靴下を裏返しにはいてるよ。

ex.en: There is a hole in your sock.
ex.ja: 靴下に穴が開いているよ。

ex.en: You have your right sock on wrong side out.
ex.ja: 右の靴下が裏返しだよ。

note.ja: ラテン語 soccus（軽い靴）から古英語に入った語。「靴下」。

en: Something added; especially, such an addition added to make up for a deficiency.
An extension to a document or publication that adds information, corrects errors, or brings up to date.
To provide or make a supplement to something.

supplement.ety: From Latin supplementum (“that which is added to supply a shortage”), from supplere (“to provide something”).

ex.en: You had better supplement your diet with vitamins.
ex.ja: あなたの食事にはビタミンを補うほうがよい。

ex.en: Farmers often moonlight to supplement their incomes.
ex.ja: 農民はしばしば収入を補うために副業をします。

note.ja: sup（下から）+ ple（満たす）+ ment。下から満たすもの →「補足・サプリメント・付録」。

en: By it; by that; by that means, or as a consequence of that.

thereby.ety: From Middle English therby, from Old English ðǣrbig, equivalent to there + by. Compare the parallel formation of German dabei.

ex.en: He exercised every day, thereby improving his health.
ex.ja: 彼は毎日運動し、それによって健康になった。

note.ja: there（それ）+ by（〜によって）。「それによって」。

en: The lowermost part of a doorway that one crosses to enter; a sill.
An entrance; the door or gate of a house.

threshold.ety:
From Middle English threschwolde, threscholde, from Old English þresċold, þerxold, þrexwold (“doorsill, entryway”), from Proto-Germanic *þreskudlaz, *þreskūþlijaz, *þreskwaþluz, from Proto-Germanic *þreskaną, *þreskwaną (“to thresh, (originally) to tread”), from Proto-Indo-European *terh₁- (“to rub, turn”).
Cognate with Low German Drüssel (“threshold”), dialectal German Drischaufel, Drissufle, Trüschübel (“threshold”), Danish tærskel (“threshold”), Norwegian Bokmål terskel (“threshold”), Norwegian Nynorsk treskald (“threshold”), Swedish tröskel (“threshold”), dialectal Swedish träskvald (“thre

ex.en: Tom carried Mary across the threshold.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーを抱いて敷居をまたいだ。

note.ja: 古英語 therscwold。前半は thresh（踏みつける・脱穀する）と関係するとされ、「足で踏む所」→「敷居」→「境目・しきい値」。

en: A malleable, ductile, metallic element, resistant to corrosion, with atomic number 50 and symbol Sn.
Iron or steel sheet metal that is coated with tin as an anticorrosion protectant.
Made of tin.
Made of galvanised iron or built of corrugated iron.
To place into a metal can (ie. a tin; be it tin, steel, aluminum) in order to preserve.
To cover with tin.

tin.ety: From Middle English tin, from Old English tin, from Proto-West Germanic *tin, from Proto-Germanic *tiną.

ex.en: He was playing football with an old tin.
ex.ja: 彼は古い空き缶でフットボールをして遊んでいました。

ex.en: Can you tell silver and tin apart?
ex.ja: 銀とブリキの区別がつきますか。

ex.en: Do you know the difference between silver and tin?
ex.ja: 銀とブリキの区別がつきますか。

note.ja: 古英語 tin から。「スズ」→ スズめっきの「ブリキ・缶」。

en: Of or relating to tribes.
Based on or organized according to tribes.
A design or image that has been influenced by indigenous peoples; especially such a tattoo.
A member of a tribe.

tribal.ety: From Latin tribālis. By surface analysis, tribe + -al, first attested in the 1630s. The specific adjectival sense under the defunct theory of recapitulation derives from tribal history as an overly literal learned borrowing from German Stammesgeschichte; ordinarily, Stamm would only be translated as tribe when used in its ethnographic sense.

ex.en: The tribal leaders met to discuss the problem.
ex.ja: 部族の長たちが集まってその問題を話し合った。

note.ja: tribe（部族）+ -al。「部族の」。

en: The usually single, more or less upright part of a tree, between the roots and the branches.
The torso; especially, the human torso.
To extract (ores) from the slimes in which they are contained, by means of a trunk.
To provide simultaneous network access to multiple clients by sharing a set of circuits, carriers, channels, or frequencies.

trunk.ety: From Middle English tronke, trunke, from Old French tronc (“alms box, tree trunk, headless body”), from Latin truncus (“a stock, lopped tree trunk”), from truncus (“cut off, maimed, mutilated”). For the verb, compare French tronquer, and see truncate. Doublet of truncus and tronk.

ex.en: Could you put these bags in the trunk?
ex.ja: この荷物をトランクにいれてもらえますか。

ex.en: The label is attached to the trunk.
ex.ja: 荷札がトランクについている。

ex.en: The trunk was too heavy for him to manage.
ex.ja: そのトランクは重すぎて彼は扱いかねた。

note.ja: ラテン語 truncus（枝を切った幹）から。「幹」→ 幹のような箱 →「大型かばん・車のトランク」、幹のように長い →「象の鼻」。truncate（切り詰める）。

en: Doubt; the condition of being uncertain or without conviction.
Something uncertain or ambiguous.

uncertainty.ety: From Middle English uncerteynte; equivalent to un- + certainty or uncertain + -ty.

ex.en: Last year was a period of economic uncertainty.
ex.ja: 昨年は経済的に不確実な時代でした。

ex.en: The evidence left no room for uncertainty.
ex.ja: その証拠で疑いの余地はなくなった。

ex.en: I feel the uncertainty of life.
ex.ja: 人生の無常をしみじみと感じる。

note.ja: un（否定）+ certain（確かな）+ -ty。certain はラテン語 cernere（ふるい分ける・見分ける）から。「見分けがつかない状態」。

en: A mythological creature (usually humanoid and undead) said to feed on the blood or life energy of the living.
A person with habits traditionally ascribed to (literal) vampires, such as heliophobia, being a night owl, having pale skin, and so on.
To drain of energy or resources.

ex.en: Do you believe in vampires?

ex.en: Tom believes in vampires.
ex.ja: トムって吸血鬼を信じてるのよ。

ex.en: A vampire can paralyze people just by looking at them.
ex.ja: 吸血鬼は睨むだけで人を金縛りにする。

note.ja: ハンガリー語・セルビア語 vampir から。スラブ語の言葉とされる。「吸血鬼」。
